keywords.def: person who studies or grows plants like flowers, fruit and vegetables
thorough understanding of a subject, gained from experience and study, that goes beyond the basic facts
searching a wide area with your eyes to find some particular thing
above and beyond what is expected; when referring to certainty, it means without any doubt
negative belief about something which is unfair or untrue
act with care and attention to avoid possible risks or dangers; be careful

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English 节目。

sentences.en: I'm Pippa. And I'm Beth. Foraging is the activity of walking in the countryside, looking for plants you can eat that grow in the wild.
sentences.zh: 我是 Pippa。我是 Beth。觅食（Foraging）是指在乡间漫步，寻找生长在野外的可食用植物。

sentences.en: That's anything from blackberries and chestnuts to mushrooms and wild garlic.
sentences.zh: 从黑莓、栗子到蘑菇和野蒜，什么都有。

sentences.en: It's something humans have always done and recently it's become fashionable among groups of young people.
sentences.zh: 这是人类一直在做的事情，最近在年轻人中变得流行起来。

sentences.en: Pippa, have you ever been foraging? Yes, we used to go and pick blackberries when I was younger, but I haven't really done it as an adult, and I would be a bit nervous to look for mushrooms or things like that.
sentences.zh: Pippa，你以前去觅食过吗？是的，我小时候经常去摘黑莓，但成年后就没怎么做过了，而且寻找蘑菇之类的东西会让我有点紧张。

sentences.en: What about you? I'm exactly the same. If I see a blackberry on a bush, I will eat it!
sentences.zh: 你呢？我也完全一样。如果我在灌木丛中看到黑莓，我会吃掉它！

sentences.en: But mushrooms? No. Too scary. So, in this episode, we'll meet two young women from different countries who are passionate about foraging wild food.
sentences.zh: 但蘑菇？不。太可怕了。所以，在本期节目中，我们将结识两位来自不同国家、热衷于寻找野食的年轻女性。

sentences.en: They're both self-taught, having learned to forage by studying the natural world around them, and it's important to say that they only eat what they can identify with one hundred percent certainty, sticking to the rule, "If in doubt leave it out!"
sentences.zh: 她们都是自学成才，通过研究周围的自然世界来学习觅食，而且重要的是，她们只吃那些能百分之百确定的东西，坚持“如有疑虑，切勿食用”的原则。

sentences.en: We'll also be learning some useful new words and phrases, all of which you'll find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们还将学习一些有用的新单词和短语，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到这些内容。

sentences.en: But before that, I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，我有一个问题要问你，Pippa。

sentences.en: As mentioned, when foraging you must know for certain what is safe to eat.
sentences.zh: 正如提到的，在野外觅食时，你必须确切知道什么是可以安全食用的。

sentences.en: Something definitely not safe to eat is the mushroom Death Cap.
sentences.zh: 绝对不能食用的一种东西是毒鹅膏菌（Death Cap）。

sentences.en: As the name suggests, it's one of the world's deadliest mushrooms, and it's common across the British Isles, but what colour is it?
sentences.zh: 顾名思义，它是世界上最致命的蘑菇之一，在不列颠群岛很常见，但它是什么颜色的呢？

sentences.en: Are Death Cap mushrooms: a) brown, b) white, or c) red?
sentences.zh: 毒鹅膏菌是：a) 棕色，b) 白色，还是 c) 红色？

sentences.en: I'm going to say, if it's dangerous maybe it's red.
sentences.zh: 我想说，如果它很危险，也许它是红色的。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。稍后我们将在节目中揭晓答案。

sentences.en: First, let's meet Roushanna Gray, a wild-food forager living in Cape Point, South Africa.
sentences.zh: 首先，让我们认识一下居住在南非开普角的野食采集者 Roushanna Gray。

sentences.en: Roushanna learned how to forage from her mother-in-law, as she explains here to BBC World Service programme The Conversation: So, she is a horticulturalist.
sentences.zh: Roushanna 是从她婆婆那里学会觅食的，正如她在 BBC World Service 节目 The Conversation 中解释的那样：所以，她是一名园艺学家。

sentences.en: She has a deep knowledge of plants. And so, I would be, kind of, scanning the landscape and learning about these new plants – or new to me – and wondering if you could eat them.
sentences.zh: 她对植物有很深的造诣。所以，我会观察周围的环境，了解这些新植物——或者对我来说是新的——并想知道是否可以食用它们。

sentences.en: Something that's incredibly important in foraging is to know a hundred and ten percent if you can eat it – positive identification of the plant.
sentences.zh: 在觅食中非常重要的一点是，要百分之百地确定是否可以食用——对植物进行准确识别。

sentences.en: And so, she was my plant person. Roushanna's mother-in-law is a horticulturalist – a person who studies or grows plants such as flowers, fruits and vegetables.
sentences.zh: 所以，她是我的植物向导。Roushanna 的婆婆是一名园艺学家（horticulturalist）——研究或种植花卉、水果和蔬菜等植物的人。

sentences.en: She has a deep knowledge of the wild plants growing in nature.
sentences.zh: 她对自然界中生长的野生植物有着深厚的知识。

sentences.en: A deep knowledge means a thorough understanding of a subject gained from experience and study, not just knowing the basic facts.
sentences.zh: “深厚的知识”（deep knowledge）意味着通过经验和学习对某一学科有透彻的理解，而不仅仅是了解基本事实。

sentences.en: One skill foragers need is scanning the landscape.
sentences.zh: 采集者需要的一项技能是观察环境（scanning the landscape）。

sentences.en: Scanning means searching a wide area with your eyes to find some particular thing – in this case, edible plants and herbs.
sentences.zh: “观察”（Scanning）意味着用眼睛搜索广阔的区域以寻找特定的东西——在这种情况下，是可食用的植物和草药。

sentences.en: And of course, Roushanna only eats plants that she can positively identify – plants that she knows a hundred and ten percent are safe to eat.
sentences.zh: 当然，Roushanna 只吃她能准确识别的植物——她百分之百确定可以安全食用的植物。

sentences.en: Here, the idiom a hundred and ten percent means Roushanna is completely sure.
sentences.zh: 在这里，习语“百分之一百一十”（a hundred and ten percent）意味着 Roushanna 完全确定。

sentences.en: She has no doubt. And that's important, as the consequences of eating poisonous plants are serious – sickness or even death.
sentences.zh: 她毫无疑问。这很重要，因为食用有毒植物的后果很严重——生病甚至死亡。

sentences.en: Our second female forager, Emily Smith, moved to rural Japan to work on a project cataloguing and collecting wild mushrooms.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位女性采集者 Emily Smith 搬到了日本农村，从事一个对野生蘑菇进行分类和收集的项目。

sentences.en: With around 5,000 varieties, 300 of which are edible, mushrooms are an important part of traditional Japanese cooking.
sentences.zh: 日本有大约 5000 个品种，其中 300 种可食用，蘑菇是日本传统烹饪的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: But with names like Death Cap and a reputation for being poisonous, mushrooms are what many wild foragers worry about the most.
sentences.zh: 但由于像“毒鹅膏菌”这样的名字以及有毒的名声，蘑菇是许多野外采集者最担心的。

sentences.en: Emily discussed these worries with BBC World Service programme The Conversation.
sentences.zh: Emily 在 BBC World Service 节目 The Conversation 中讨论了这些担忧。

sentences.en: That stigma is a bit misplaced, I think, because plants can be just as dangerous, if not more dangerous than mushrooms, and I think that mushrooms have been much maligned.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种偏见有点不对，因为植物可能和蘑菇一样危险，甚至更危险，而且我认为蘑菇一直被严重诋毁了。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got to exercise caution, as Roushanna said, in anything that you pick.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如 Roushanna 所说，采摘任何东西都必须谨慎行事。

sentences.en: You need to know what it is before you consume it.
sentences.zh: 在食用之前，你需要知道它是什么。

sentences.en: "If in doubt, throw it out!" is a very good phrase to say.
sentences.zh: “如有疑虑，扔掉它！”是一句非常好的话。

sentences.en: Emily thinks there's a stigma around mushrooms.
sentences.zh: Emily 认为人们对蘑菇存在偏见。

sentences.en: A stigma is a negative belief about something which is not necessarily true or fair.
sentences.zh: “污名”（stigma）是指对某事物的负面看法，这种看法不一定真实或公平。

sentences.en: In fact, many plants are just as poisonous as mushrooms.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多植物和蘑菇一样有毒。

sentences.en: The main thing is to exercise caution – to act with care and attention so as to avoid possible dangers.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是“谨慎行事”（exercise caution）——小心谨慎地行动，以避免可能的危险。

sentences.en: In other words, to be careful. And the best way of doing that is learning the difference between what's safe to eat and what's not.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是要小心。而最好的办法就是学习如何区分什么是安全食用的，什么不是。

sentences.en: Speaking of which, what was the answer to your question, Beth?
sentences.zh: 说到这里，Beth，你那个问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: Ah! I asked you, "What colour are Death Cap mushrooms?" You said red, which I also thought was the answer, but actually they are white.
sentences.zh: 啊！我问你，“毒鹅膏菌是什么颜色的？”你说是红色，我也曾以为是这个答案，但实际上它们是白色的。

sentences.en: Right, it's time to recap the vocabulary we've learnt about foraging, starting with horticulturalist – a person who studies or grows plants.
sentences.zh: 好了，是时候回顾一下我们学过的关于觅食的词汇了，首先是园艺学家（horticulturalist）——研究或种植植物的人。

sentences.en: If you have a deep knowledge of a subject, you have a thorough understanding of it, gained from experience and study.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某一学科有“深厚的知识”（deep knowledge），你就通过经验和学习对其有了透彻的理解。

sentences.en: Scanning involves searching a wide area with your eyes to find some particular thing.
sentences.zh: “观察”（Scanning）包括用眼睛搜索广阔的区域以寻找特定的东西。

sentences.en: If you're a hundred and ten percent sure about something, you're absolutely certain.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某件事“百分之一百一十确定”（hundred and ten percent sure），你就是绝对肯定。

sentences.en: You have no doubt. A stigma is an unfair, negative belief about something.
sentences.zh: 你毫无疑问。“污名”（stigma）是指对某事物不公平的负面看法。

sentences.en: And finally, to exercise caution is a more formal way of saying to be careful – something you should definitely remember if you go wild foraging yourself!
sentences.zh: 最后，“谨慎行事”（exercise caution）是“小心”的一种更正式的表达方式——如果你自己去野外觅食，一定要记住这一点！

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you enjoyed this episode, you'll find a quiz and worksheet to practise the vocabulary on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了。如果你喜欢本期节目，可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到测验和工作表来练习词汇。

sentences.en: See you again soon. Bye for now! Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见。再见！再见！
